thread:
sarah: Thanks everyone — quick follow-ups from today's all-hands runtime segment. Wanted a concise thread to capture clarifications on fallbacks, SLOs, and the kernel rollout timeline.
jamie: thanks — two quick asks: 1) what are the literal SLO targets we want public in the playbook (p50/p95/p99) for hosted vs dedicated? 2) any hard constraints on fallback behavior (e.g., auto-quantize then route)?
mike: re: kernels — kernel-v4 rollout is gated on perf regression tests we finish next week. If those pass, staged canary in two weeks. No full-prod date yet.
nate: SLO targets proposal from infra: hosted p50=20ms, p95=120ms, p99=400ms. Dedicated: p50=15ms, p95=80ms, p99=250ms. These include network hop overhead assumptions.
liz: product ask — can we keep a public-facing "best-effort" bucket for non-SLA customers that will accept fallbacks to cheaper quantized models? We want clear messaging for customers.
jamie: +1 to a documented "best-effort" tier. For fallbacks, operations wants an ordered policy: 1) route to same-model quantized variant, 2) route to compatible smaller architecture, 3) degrade features (no streaming). Is that policy ok?
sarah: that ordering makes sense. Two constraints: no silent semantic regressions for top-tier customers, and any fallback must be observable in telemetry and traced.
mike: agreed. Also proposing a lightweight config block we can ship in the console for canary toggles and fallback policy. Example snippet:
```
fallback_policy:
  priority: [quantized_same, smaller_compatible, degraded_features]
  max_latency_ms: 1000
  track_regressions: true
```
jamie: +1. Also need to clarify KV cache eviction strategy. Today we TTL at 5m by default; ops asked for adaptive eviction. We could implement LRU with a recency-weighted TTL that extends hot prefixes. Thoughts?
nate: adaptive makes sense. Ops action: we'll run a 2-week experiment toggling hot-prefix retention to 20m and report cost delta. If cost delta < 8% and p95 latency improves for common prompts, recommend enabling.
liz: can marketing/product owners get a short blurb about the fallback guarantees so we can update docs and onboarding?
sarah: yes — jamie and nate, please draft a 2-paragraph blurb by EOD Friday. Ops-bot will add the meeting notes link when you post.
ops-bot: Meeting notes uploaded: https://redwood.internal/notes/allhands-2630012345 (access: eng+product). :white_check_mark:
jamie: action items: 1) draft blurb (jamie, nate) 2) kernel-v4 perf runs (mike) 3) run hot-prefix retention experiment (nate) 4) add fallback toggle config to console backlog (eng-platform). I'll post a short RFC thread after lunch.
mike: FYI — perf runs will include end-to-end p95 across typical seq-lens (32/128/512). I'll share numbers in RFC.
sarah: perfect. thanks everyone — if you have blockers, ping me directly.
